title: Space
seo_title: Year 7 Science: Space Worksheets (Stars, Galaxies, Light Years, Seasons)
standard_text: Gravity force, weight = mass × gravitational field strength (g), on Earth g=10 N/kg, different on other planets and stars; gravity forces between Earth and Moon, and between Earth and Sun (qualitative only); our Sun as a star, other stars in our galaxy, other galaxies; the seasons and the Earth's tilt, day length at different times of year, in different hemispheres; the light year as a unit of astronomical distance.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 science worksheets on space: the Sun as a star, galaxies, the light year, the planets, gravity and why we have seasons in each hemisphere. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The Sun is a star in the Milky Way.
key_sub: A light year is a distance. The Earth's tilt causes the seasons.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Sun is one star in the Milky Way, one of billions of galaxies.

  • A light year is the distance light travels in a year, about 9.5 million million km.
  • Seasons happen because the Earth's axis is tilted, not because the Earth gets closer to the Sun.
  • Gravity keeps the Moon orbiting the Earth and the planets orbiting the Sun.
Example

A star 8.6 light years away. Light takes?

A light year is a distance

Answer: 8.6 years

Example

July in the UK. Season in Australia?

Opposite hemispheres

Answer: winter

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a light year is a unit of time.
  • Thinking summer happens because the Earth is closer to the Sun.
  • Thinking the Sun is the biggest star.
